question: In the pulverized-coal boiler, why did burnout-zone ammonia injection give the lowest NO of the 20% cofiring cases?
expect: premise false: flame-zone injection gives the lowest NO; burnout-zone injection gives the largest NO penalty (about +571%) (abstract)
rendered:
document title="Ammonia Co-Firing in a Staged-Air Pulverized-Coal Boiler: Reactor-Network Prediction of Carbon Reduction and Nitrogen-Oxide Emissions"

The answer is: Because intense coal combustion in the main section consumes substantial O2, and the overfire air admitted to the burnout zone is insufficient for the large NH3 load; consequently, incomplete combustion products increase and CO, CO2, and NO concentrations exceed those of the other injection cases.
